back: $R(h)=\mathbb E\,\ell(h(x),y)$ over the data distribution; $\hat R_n(h)=\frac1n\sum_i\ell(h(x_i),y_i)$ on the sample. Gap $=R-\hat R_n$.

front: Why is the ERM training error optimistic?
back: The hypothesis is selected using the data; the best-looking one among many benefits from luck. A hypothesis fixed in advance has an unbiased empirical risk.
$P(\cup A_j)\le\sum_jP(A_j)$. It turns a per-hypothesis guarantee into a guarantee over all $M$ hypotheses, at the cost of a factor $M$ in the failure probability.
With probability $\ge1-\delta$, for all $h$: $|R-\hat R_n|\le\sqrt{\ln(2M/\delta)/(2n)}$. Grows like $\sqrt{\ln M}$.

front: ERM excess risk for a finite class
back: $R(\hat h)\le R(h^\star)+2\varepsilon$ where $\varepsilon$ is the uniform deviation width.
A set of $m$ points is shattered if the class realises all $2^m$ labelings of it.
Largest $d$ such that SOME set of $d$ points is shattered. Needs one shattered example and an impossibility proof for $d+1$.

front: VC dimension of intervals; half-planes in $\mathbb R^2$
back: Intervals on a line: 2 (labeling 1,0,1 impossible). Half-planes in the plane: 3; in $\mathbb R^p$ linear classifiers with bias: $p+1$.
Growth function $\Pi(n)\le(en/d)^d$ for $n\ge d$: labelings grow polynomially, not exponentially, beyond the VC dimension.
$R\le\hat R_n+\sqrt{(d(\ln(2n/d)+1)+\ln(4/\delta))/n}$ (constants vary): penalty about $\sqrt{d\ln n/n}$, so want $n\gg d$.
$\mathbb E_\sigma\max_h\frac1n\sum_i\sigma_ih(x_i)$: how well the class fits random $\pm1$ labels. 0 for one hypothesis, 1 if it can realise every labeling.
For $M$ hypotheses with values $\pm1$: Rademacher complexity $\le\sqrt{2\ln M/n}$.
SRM: nested classes, minimise training error plus a complexity penalty. Regularisation $\hat R_n+\lambda\Omega(h)$ is the continuous version (e.g. $\|w\|^2$).

front: No free lunch and deep nets
back: No algorithm wins on all problems, so assumptions are needed. For deep nets the uniform VC bound is vacuous yet they generalise; the explanation is an open research area.
